title: config.json — the mod's settings for one game
description: What the mod writes beside its translation for one game, read by the mod at every launch and by the Manager to show and change a game's setup. Every key is therefore an agreement between two programs, and every migration below is what keeps a file written a year ago meaning what its owner meant. `x-writer` says who writes a key: `mod` (the mod alone), `both` (the Manager writes it too, through GameConfigWriter.Intended — the sub-contract a Core must honour to be configurable by the Manager), `manager-reads` (read by the Manager, never written by it), `migration` (read once, then removed). The schema describes the CURRENT written form (config_version 3, every key present as the mod serialises them); older forms and the keys they carried are `x-migrations`, and a file carrying one is `written: false` and still read.
x-secrets: api_token, ai_api_key, google_api_key, deepl_api_key, proxy_password are stored as `ENCRYPTED:` + base64(IV ‖ AES-256-CBC), keyed to the machine (common/Secrets: PBKDF2-SHA1 100 000 iterations over MachineName_UserName_Platform_UGT_v3, salt SHA-256 of MachineName_UserName_UGT_SALT). A value WITHOUT the prefix is read in the clear and re-encrypted at the next save — how a secret saved by an older version keeps working. A value with the prefix that does not decrypt on this machine reads as no secret, never as corruption. The Manager encrypts with the same scheme so the mod can read what it wrote.

x-migrations.how: copied; the old key is dropped
the file predates the backend choice; AI on meant llm
every older file carried an explicit false the mod had serialised itself; false now means a decision, so it goes back to undecided — once

x-migrations.from: config_version < 2, enable_ai: false with translation_backend google|deepl
x-migrations.how: the flag used to mean 'the backend is llm' and was false for the paid backends; read for what it meant. NOT applied to llm, where false already meant off
the key was serialised and read by nothing; 30000 is a default nobody chose. Any other value is a real choice and is kept
read once, then removed from the file

x-migrations.to: 1h, and sync.realtime_own_translation: true for auto and realtime, false otherwise
x-migrations.how: one setting became two; decided from the value AS STORED, only when realtime_own_translation is ABSENT from the raw file. An unknown value reads as 1h, never as never
ignored on read, dropped at the next save

translation_backend.description: WHICH service translates — never WHETHER (that is enable_ai). ⚠ The Manager's own 'capture' choice is written here as `none` with capture_keys_only true; the mod never sees 'capture'.

ai_url.description: OpenAI-compatible server. ONE spelling of local, 127.0.0.1, never localhost (common/Endpoints).

target_language.description: A catalogue NAME (French), never an ISO code; `auto` is a MODE resolved against the machine's system language and settled by the translation's first line. The Manager writes it only when the game has none (OnlyIfAbsent), and never `auto`.

source_language.description: The language the game's own text is in. `auto` = unknown. The Manager writes it on ONE path only — taking a published translation, whose pair its author stated — and never from a list of settings: a wrong guess is an instruction to the model, and with strict_source_language it retires lines for good.

game_context.description: What the game is about, sent to the model. The Manager writes it only when it holds one for this game, never clears it by omission.

timeout_ms.description: How long ONE backend request may take. Five minutes on purpose: a busy local model answers in minutes and every one of those answers came back.

enable_ai.description: WHETHER live translation runs, whichever backend is selected. Written by the Manager for every backend; false when it chose 'capture'.

deepl_use_free.description: Free and paid DeepL are different hosts.

rate_limit_retry_delay.description: Seconds before retrying after a 429, any backend.

ai_max_attempts.description: Requests one line may cost, at most, for a repair or a retranslation. Clamped to 1..10 on read, never trusted from the file (Placeholders.MaxAttempts is the default).

ai_temperature.description: Zero on purpose: the answer is cached and shared. Clamped to 0..2 on read.

config_version.description: Which one-shot migrations have run; a current Core writes the current number, nothing else (0 = written before migrations were versioned, and any older number is a file still to migrate — `written: false`, still read). Bumping it here and in ModConfig.CurrentConfigVersion is one change.

capture_keys_only.description: Collect the game's text without translating it. The Manager writes it either way (true for 'capture', false otherwise).

translate_mod_ui.description: THREE states: true/false = the person decided; null = let the translation decide.

first_run_completed.description: The wizard has been answered. The Manager writes true only when its settings answer every question the wizard asks, and REMOVES the key (never writes false) to let the game ask again: absent is 'never answered', false would be a claim.

online_mode.description: Community features in game: search, sync, publishing.

settings_hotkey.description: Opens the mod's panel. A key name with optional modifiers (`Ctrl+Alt+F10`). The Manager writes only UNIVERSAL keys (common/BindableKeys): what a KeyCode designates depends on a per-project Unity setting no runtime reports, and a key that prints a character means different things in different games. Written on a fresh config, and afterwards only on demand.

api_token.description: The bearer token the device flow delivered (`ugt_…`). Never touched by the Manager: a credential belongs to the program its owner handed it to.

api_user.description: Who the mod is signed in as, in this game. Set and cleared with the token. The Manager reads it — one machine carries several accounts — and never writes it.

api_token_server.description: The server that issued the token. When api_base_url changes, the token, api_user and this are cleared: a token must not be replayed against another server.

api_base_url.description: Self-hosting override; null = the compiled default.

proxy_mode.description: The Manager carries its proxy into games only when asked and only when its own mode is not default.

sync.description: The Manager writes its keys ONE AT A TIME, so everything else the block holds survives.

update_check_frequency.description: The rhythm of the checks, and nothing else. Every rhythm also checks once at startup.

realtime_own_translation.description: Keep a stream open for what THIS account publishes elsewhere — one's own line only. A permission: opened only when there is something of one's own to watch.

dismissed_notices.description: Notices shown once and dismissed, as `type:uuid`.

notify_prereleases.description: The Manager writes true when its channel is beta, and reads it back as the channel (true → beta, false → stable, absent → unknown).
